prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (RDC, call sign Juniper) intakes EMS requests, preserves incident record incl original caller report, clarifications/estimates, location, medical details, priority, assignments, route/destination changes; supports triage, dispatch, coordination, shared picture. Aliases: Call Taker Mara=Larkspur; Triage Supervisor=Copperfield; Shift Commander=Sundial; Radio Coordinator=Mistral. Jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy; zones/routes reviewed for road/population/agreement changes. CAD/dispatch decisions consider distance, access, travel time, restrictions, weather, closures, queue congestion, demand, capacity, crew readiness, unit capability, coverage. Larkspur enters/updates incident data and confirms incident ID/intended receiving facility before destination request; sends/uses correction slip/Caller Location Correction Slip to reconcile location or destination changes. Copperfield assigns/confirms priority, records basis, confirms response level, sends Pediatric Acuity Note, advises repositioning when clinical demand changes. Regional Medical Director sets clinical policy/priorities and guidance/limits, incl elevated demand and specialized capability/regional protocol destinations; no operational dispatch authority. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates position/status, presents matching units, retains time-stamped status changes, and presents approved destination/instructions. RDC uses swap voucher to confirm battery readiness before placing unit in service; uses queue snapshot before northern routing. North Gate Status Board displays latest queue condition/access restriction for northern entry. Dispatchers compare projected response times with remaining coverage before moving units; route alternatives are approved/recorded only after coverage check. Crews acknowledge/repeat location/priority, report status/position and route unsuitability from closure/unsafe condition/delay; discrepancies require fresh transmission. Mistral manages radio/talkgroups, transmits incident ID/location/priority/assignment/hazards, confirms route changes, retries no-ack, sends Coverage Gap Bulletin. Sundial reviews coverage, approves exceptions/nonstandard response, sends Mutual Aid Release Form when neighboring service released. Hospital Liaison Desk provides facility capacity, coordinates destination consultation using patient condition, transport estimate, facility acceptance; contacts Emergency Department, records outcome, communicates restrictions to RDC. Emergency Department reports capacity limits/access constraints/receiving-status changes. Data Quality Officer reviews inconsistent location/status reports and routes corrections through operational process.

New part:
S159: The Radio Coordinator relays destination instructions to the Paramedic Crew over the Regional Radio Network.
S160: The Paramedic Crew acknowledges the destination and advises dispatch if conditions require renewed consultation.
S161: The South Gate Status Board produces the South Access Lane Notice when the south approach has a material access constraint.
S162: The South Gate Status Board displays current access information for crews approaching the receiving facility through the south entrance.
S163: The Shift Commander reviews access constraints that could affect arrival timing or safe patient transfer.
S164: The Regional Radio Network supports updates between dispatch and the Paramedic Crew while the ambulance is en route.
S165: Call Taker Mara receives the Bedside Arrival Receipt to support completion of the incident record.
S166: Call Taker Mara verifies that the recorded arrival time is consistent with the dispatch timeline and crew communications.
S167: Ambulance Unit 417 reports arrival at the receiving facility and confirms when patient handover is complete.
S168: The Emergency Department and the Paramedic Crew clarify any discrepancy in patient identity or transfer documentation before the crew clears the facility.
S169: The Data Quality Officer reviews incomplete arrival or handover fields during routine record-quality checks.
S170: The Regional Dispatch Center updates the incident status after receiving confirmation that the patient has been transferred to facility care.
S171: The Hospital Liaison Desk remains available to resolve facility-level questions that arise during or immediately after handover.
S172: The Shift Commander escalates unresolved destination or access issues through established regional coordination procedures.
S173: Surge operations begin when queue age, simultaneous high-priority calls, or staffed unit availability crosses thresholds approved by regional policy.
S174: Regional Dispatch Center monitors these indicators continuously and declares the applicable surge level when a threshold is met.
S175: Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays the current surge level and the operational constraints reported by field and facility staff.
S176: Triage Supervisor validates the declaration and confirms that call prioritization remains consistent with clinical protocols.
S177: Shift Commander assigns coordination responsibilities and reviews whether normal coverage can be maintained during the surge.
S178: Regional Medical Director provides clinical direction when demand exceeds routine triage guidance or requires a regional protocol adjustment.
S179: Hospital Liaison Desk uses the Pediatric Acuity Note to convey pediatric monitoring and destination considerations to receiving staff.
S180: Pediatric calls with concerning airway, breathing, circulation, or mental status findings receive prompt clinical escalation under approved protocols.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
